IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r5.claim: The source states that there is no reading disagreement throughout Sūrat al-Jumuʿa.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r5.anchor: سورة الجمعة لم يختلفوا فى سورة الجمعة

NAHHAS:v4p425/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p425/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p425/r5.claim: يتلو عليهم is an accusative circumstantial phrase modifying رسول.
NAHHAS:v4p425/r5.anchor: في موضع نصب أي تاليا عليهم نعت لرسول

NAHHAS:v4p425/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p425/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p425/r6.claim: To purify them means to call them to obedience; when they obey, they have become purified.
NAHHAS:v4p425/r6.anchor: معنى يزكيهم يدعوهم إلى طاعة الله عز وجل فإذا أطاعوه فقد تزكوا وزكاهم

NAHHAS:v4p425/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p425/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p425/r7.claim: The two lām letters may be assimilated.

ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r3.claim: The ummiyyūn cannot write and remain as the community was created before learning scripture, which requires instruction.
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r3.anchor: (الأميين) الذين لا يكتبون، الذين هم على ما خلقت عليه الأمة

ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r4.claim: Someone who has not learned reading but recites what he heard is said to read by innate nature; the listed synonyms all mean nature.
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r4.anchor: وقولهم في الذي لا يعرف الكلام ولا القراءة: هو يقرأ بالسليقة، أي لم يتعلم القراءة معربا إنما يقرأ على ما سمع الكلام

ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r5.speaker: أهل الطائف
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r5.claim: One account says writing began among the Arabs at al-Ṭāʾif; its people say they learned from al-Ḥīrah, whose people say they learned from al-Anbār.
ZAJJAJ:v5p169/r5.anchor: وقيل أول ما بدأ الكتاب في العرب بدا من أهل الطائف، وذكر أهل الطائف أنهم تعلموا الكتابة في أهل الحيرة، وذكر أهل الحيرة أنهم تعلموا الكتابة من أهل الأنبار.

ASAD-NOTES:62:2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:62:2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:62:2/r1.claim: God sent an apostle from among the unlettered people to recite His messages, purify them and teach scripture and wisdom, since they had been manifestly astray.
ASAD-NOTES:62:2/r1.anchor: to convey unto them His messages, and to cause them to grow in purity, and to impart unto them the divine writ as well as wisdom

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p948/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p948/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p948/r3.claim: In al-Jumuʿa, the tasbih opening is followed by God's sending a messenger from among the unlettered to recite, purify, and teach them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p948/r3.anchor: هُوَ الَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آَيَاتِهِ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p313/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p313/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p313/r2.claim: The preceding sūrah recalls Jesus’ prediction about Muhammad; al-Jumu‘ah alludes to Abraham’s prayer for the Ishmaelites.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p313/r2.anchor: This sūrah alludes to the prayer of Abraham

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p313/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p313/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p313/r3.claim: The Ishmaelites must honour God’s favor of sending Muhammad among them and resist Jewish conspiracies that could deprive them of it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p313/r3.anchor: and to not deprive themselves of this great blessing by being misled by the conspiracies of the Jews.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r3.claim: The Messenger is sent to manifest God’s attributes: as Sovereign, God informs creation of His directives through a Messenger who recites His teachings and guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r3.anchor: the Messenger mentioned in this verse was sent forth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r4.claim: Because God is pure and flawless, He sent His Messenger and teachings to purify people’s beliefs and deeds and cleanse moral evils.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r4.anchor: He is pure and flawless, and for this reason He wanted to purify people through His Messenger and His teachings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r5.claim: Al-kitāb means sharī‘ah or divine law, whose enforcement requires power and authority; God’s wisdom makes that law express people’s welfare in this life and the next, not force alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r5.anchor: The word al-kitāb here means the sharī‘ah or the divine law. The sharī‘ah can only be enforced by someone who is powerful and has authority.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r6.claim: The designation “unlettered” distinguishes the Ishmaelites; Islahi says Jews coined it to express religious arrogance and derision toward Arabia’s people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p315/r6.anchor: this term was actually coined specifically by the Jews among the People of the Book which reflected their religious arrogance as well as derision for the people of Arabia

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r1.claim: Though unfamiliar with divine law, the Ishmaelites adopted “unlettered” as a title without inferiority; Qur’anic use raised it into a mark of divinely given respect.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r1.anchor: they themselves adopted this term as a title without any inferiority complex

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r2.claim: God’s providence reversed the status of a people once disparaged: they were entrusted with guiding the whole world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r2.anchor: they, who were derided and disparaged were entrusted with the responsibility of instructing and guiding the whole world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r4.claim: The designation also stirs gratitude: God sent a person from among the Ishmaelites to reform and educate them in law and wisdom, lifting them from jāhiliyyah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r4.anchor: For their own reformation and instruction and to educate them in law and wisdom, He sent forth among them a person from among themselves

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r5.claim: The recipients should value and honour this favour and encourage others to do likewise, lest they lose it and vindicate the envious.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r5.anchor: they who have received this favour should value and honour it, and also try that others adopt this attitude as well

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r6.claim: Islahi directs readers to his earlier Baqarah discussion of the unlettered Prophet’s attributes to address rejecters of Hadith who misunderstand his mission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r6.anchor: Readers are advised to look it up so that the misunderstandings which have been spread by the rejecters of Ḥadīth regarding the purpose of his advent are dispelled.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r7.claim: Abraham prayed for an Ishmaelite messenger with the same tasks named in 62:2: reciting revelation, teaching law and wisdom, and purifying the people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r7.anchor: Abraham (sws) had prayed to God to send forth a prophet among the Ishmaelites having exactly these attributes.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r8.claim: Muhammad manifests both God’s attributes and Abraham’s prayer, and combines several distinct attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r8.anchor: just as Muḥammad (sws) is a manifestation of the attributes of God, he is also a manifestation of the prayer of Abraham (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r9.claim: Muhammad fulfills Jesus’ prediction and Abraham’s prayer while reflecting God’s attributes as a human being from among the unlettered Arabs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r9.anchor: He is the realization of Jesus’ prediction and the manifestation of Abraham’s prayer. He is also a reflection of God’s attributes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r10.claim: Because the Messenger was no alien to the Arabs, their detractors cannot claim they received guidance through another people; God elevated them to carry guidance to the world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r10.anchor: He is no stranger or alien to them. Those who are belittling them cannot blame them that they received the light of guidance through them or through some other means

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r1.claim: The Prophet’s specific mission to the Ishmaelites was completed by him; his universal mission to humanity continues through his followers, witnesses to truth until Judgment, with the Ishmaelites as vanguard.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r1.anchor: The former related to the Ishmaelites and the obligations of this prophethood were brought a completion by the Prophet (sws) himself. The latter related to all mankind

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r2.claim: The clause about their former manifest error recalls the people’s long ignorance so they recognize God’s favour in bringing them from darkness to honour.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r2.anchor: are meant to stir up feelings of gratitude in the ummiyyīn. They had been engulfed in darkness of ignorance since a long time.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r4.claim: Although “ummiyyīn” is general in wording, Islahi reads verse 2 as referring specifically to Ishmaelites who had already embraced faith; its closing clause that they were previously in manifest error supports this.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p317/r4.anchor: in the previous verse though the word ummiyyīn is used in the general sense, it referred to only those Ishmaelites who had already embraced faith

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p321/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p321/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p321/r4.claim: The incident showed that many Muslims did not appreciate God’s great blessing in sending Muḥammad to the unlettered Arabs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p321/r4.anchor: many people were not fully cognizant of the great blessing of God which He bestowed on the unlettered Arabs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p322/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p322/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p322/r4.claim: These grave weaknesses led Muslims to undervalue the blessing given to Arabia’s unlettered people, a blessing emphasized throughout the sūrah and resented by the Jews.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p322/r4.anchor: All these weaknesses were very grave

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p291/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p291/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p291/r1.claim: Qatāda says this community was unlettered and did not read a scripture.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p291/r1.anchor: عن معمر قال تلا قتادة ﴿ هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم ﴾ قال كانت هذه الأمة أمة أمية لا يقرأون كتابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p171/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p171/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p171/r7.claim: The parallel wording and the attribution of al-ummi were discussed earlier in connection with a verse in Āl ʿImrān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p171/r7.anchor: هو الذي بعث الآية: تقدم الكلام في نظيرها في آل عمران وفي نسبة الأمي

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r1.claim: The ummiyyīn are the Arabs, most of whom could neither write nor read.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r1.anchor: يعني سبحانه العرب لأن أكثرهم لا يكتبون ولا يقرأون

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying that this is an unlettered nation that neither writes nor calculates; al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i transmit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : إنا أمة أمية

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r3.claim: The best-known derivation makes ummī a relation to one's mother: the person remains in the original state of birth without learned writing or arithmetic.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r3.anchor: لم يتعلموا الكتابة والحساب فهم على جبلتهم الأولى فالأمي نسبة إلى الأم التي ولدته

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r4.claim: An alternative derives ummī from the Arab nation.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r4.anchor: وقيل نسبة إلى أمة العرب وقيل : إلى أم القرى والأول أشهر

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r5.claim: Another alternative derives ummī from Umm al-Qurā.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r5.anchor: وقيل نسبة إلى أمة العرب وقيل : إلى أم القرى والأول أشهر

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r6.claim: Some commentators restrict ummī to someone who cannot write.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r6.anchor: واقتصر بعضهم في تفسيره على أنه الذي لا يكتب

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r7.claim: Writing is said to have begun at al-Ta'if; its people learned it from people of al-Hirah, who were from al-Anbar.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r7.anchor: والكتابة على ما قيل : بدئت بالطائف أخذوها من أهل الحيرة وهم من أهل الأنبار

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r8.claim: A variant reads al-ummiyyīn with the nisba yāʾ omitted.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r9.claim: In rasūlan minhum, min is partitive and the messenger is from their group.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r9.anchor: أي كائنا من جملتهم فمن تبعيضية

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r10.claim: If the partitive relation is by genus, it does not establish that the Prophet himself was unlettered.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r10.anchor: فمن تبعيضية والبعضية : إما باعتبار الجنس فلا تدل على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أمي

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r11.speaker: جمع
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r11.claim: A group prefers the shared distinguishing quality common to most Arabs: the messenger was one of them, unlettered like them.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r11.anchor: أو باعتبار الخاصة المشتركة في الأكثر فتدل واختار هذا جمع فالمعنى رسولا من جملتهم أميا مثلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r12.claim: The Prophet recited God's signs to them despite being unlettered like them and never having been known to read or study.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r12.anchor: مع كونه أميا مثلهم لم يعهد منه قراءة ولا تعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r13.claim: Yuzakkīhim is coordinated with yatlū and is another description of the messenger; it means leading them to purity from corrupt beliefs and deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r13.anchor: فهو صفة أيضا لرسولا أي يحملهم على ما يصيرون به أزكياء طاهرين من خبائث العقائد والأعمال

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r14.claim: Teaching the Book and wisdom is also a description of the messenger and follows recitation in the order of occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r14.anchor: صفة أيضا لرسولا مترتبة في الوجود على التلاوة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r15.claim: Purification precedes teaching in the wording although practical perfection follows theoretical teaching, to show that each stage is a distinct blessing deserving thanks.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r15.anchor: وإنما وسط بينهم التزكية التي هي عبارة عن تكميل النفس بحسب قوتها العملية وتهذيبها المتفرع على تكميلها بحسب القوة النظرية

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r16.claim: Calling the Qur'an signs in one place and Book and wisdom in another signals that each aspect is a separate blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r16.anchor: وهو السر في التعبير عن القرآن تارة بالآيات وأخرى بالكتاب والحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r17.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r17.claim: One eminent scholar says wisdom includes the rulings and laws contained in Prophetic reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r17.anchor: ولا يقدح فيه شمول الحكمة لما في تضاعيف الأحاديث النبوية من الأحكام والشرائع قاله بعض الأجلة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r18.claim: Another possible reading treats Book and wisdom as a metaphor for all transmitted and rational disciplines, as heavens and earth can stand for all beings or the Helpers and Emigrants for all Companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r18.anchor: كناية عن جميع النقليات والعقليات كالسماوات والأرض بجميع الموجودات والأنصار والمهاجرين بجميع الصحابة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r19.claim: The Prophet's extensive knowledge is itself a striking miracle; the cited poet says knowledge in an unlettered man and instruction in an orphan suffice as a miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93/r19.anchor: وفيه من الدلالة على مزيد علمه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ما فيه ولو لم يكن له عليه الصلاة والسلام سوى ذلك معجزة لكفاه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r1.claim: Their former manifest error was polytheism and the corruption of jāhiliyya, demonstrating their need for guidance; error is ascribed to most, with exceptions such as Waraka.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r1.anchor: من الشرك وخبث الجاهلية وهو بيان لشدة افتقارهم إلى من يرشدهم وإن كان نسبة الضلال إليهم باعتبار الأكثر

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r2.claim: The clause also dispels a possible assumption that the Prophet learned from someone else.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r2.anchor: وفي الكلام إزاحة لما عسى أن يتوهم من تعلمه عليه الصلاة والسلام من الغير

ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p93#2/r3.claim: In is the lightened form of inna, and the lām marks it as such rather than a conditional in.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r1.claim: The ummiyyūn are the Arabs, an unlettered people who neither wrote nor read.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r1.anchor: يعني العرب كانت أمة أمية لا تكتب ولا تقرأ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r2.claim: The messenger is Muhammad, sharing their lineage and language, making the proof forceful.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r2.anchor: نسبه نسبهم [ولسانه لسانهم ليكون أبلغ في إقامة الحجة عليهم]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r3.claim: Before the Messenger, they worshipped idols and were in manifest error.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p111#2/r3.anchor: أي ما كانوا قبل بعثة الرسول إلا في ضلال مبين يعبدون الأوثان.

BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r4.claim: The unlettered are the Arabs, most of whom could neither write nor read.
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r4.anchor: أي في العرب لأن أكثرهم لا يكتبون ولا يقرؤون

BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r5.claim: The Messenger is one of their own, unlettered like them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r6.claim: His recitation of the signs by one who had never read or studied is a sign of his prophethood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r6.anchor: من كونه أميا مثلهم لم يعهد منه قراءة ولا تعلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r7.claim: He purifies them of corrupt beliefs and deeds.

BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r8.claim: The Book and Wisdom mean the Qurʾān and religious law, or the principles of religion from transmitted and rational learning; this alone would suffice as his miracle.
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r8.anchor: القرآن والشريعة، أو معالم الدين من المنقول والمعقول

BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r9.claim: Their former manifest error was idolatry and the corruption of the Jāhiliyya; this shows their need for a guiding prophet and removes the suspicion that he learned from a teacher.
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r9.anchor: من الشرك وخبث الجاهلية، وهو بيان لشدة احتياجهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r10.claim: Here إن is the lightened form of إنَّ, indicated by the lām.
BAYDAWI-FULL:62:1-2/r10.anchor: و { إن } هي المخففة واللام تدل عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p591/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p591/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p591/r3.claim: The passage praising the Messenger and his community answers the possible impression that Jesus's followers possess greater virtue.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p591/r3.anchor: هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r2.claim: Purifying rude, resistant people by making them affirm transcendence demonstrates God's power; having said Israelites refused purification and strayed, the author infers His power to purify all rational beings.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r2.anchor: ولما كانت القدرة على تزكية الجلف الجافي بحمله على التنزيه أدل على القدرة على غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r3.claim: هُوَ means God alone; بعث describes sending from the hidden presence with the law's commands and prohibitions.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r3.anchor: أي وحده { الذي بعث } أي من حضرة غيب غيبه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r4.claim: Al-ummiyyūn first means the Arabs, known among other peoples for not writing and remaining in the original, natural state of birth.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r4.anchor: أي العرب لأنهم كانوا معروفين من بين سائر الأمم لا يكتبون بل هم على الخلقة الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r5.claim: He also allows the word to include all Earth's people: knowledge had disappeared when the Prophet was sent, and Arabs are the root while other peoples follow them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تطلق الأمية على جميع أهل الأرض لأن بعثه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان حين ذهب العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r6.claim: The Messenger's being from the same people makes their reform through one of their own kind remarkable; his unlettered state is an abiding natural quality, without learned artifice, while his knowledge came without acquisition.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r6.anchor: ولما كان تقويم الشيء بمثله أعجب قال : { منهم } بل الأمة بمعنى عدم الكتابة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r7.claim: Although his mission began among the Arabs, his origin does not restrict his mission: explicit texts and decisive proofs establish that he was sent to all humanity.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r7.anchor: وذكر بعثه منهم إن خص الوصف بالعرب لا ينفي بعثه إلى غيرهم ولا سيما مع ما ورد فيه من الصرائح

BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r8.claim: يَتْلُوا means to recite one passage after another, repeatedly and with elevation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r8.anchor: { يتلوا } أي يقرأ قراءة يتبع بعضها بعضا على وجه الكثرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r9.claim: His recitation is a clear proof of his truth: though unlettered like his audience, he brings verses while many among them can write and learn, a gift only the omnipotent could grant.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p592/r9.anchor: مع كونه أميا مثلهم { آياته } أي يأتيهم بها على سبيل التجدد

BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r1.claim: Tazkiya removes base morals and deviant beliefs. In this context it precedes instruction because some had fallen into affection for disbelievers; during the Prophet's life, his loving gaze, teaching, and recitation purified people.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r1.anchor: { ويزكيهم } أي عن الأخلاق الرذيلة والعقائد الزائغة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r2.claim: Biqāʿī recounts that Umayr ibn Wahb, after plotting with Ṣafwān to kill the Prophet following Badr, was guided by him; after Mecca's conquest Umayr brought the fleeing Ṣafwān back, who then converted, and Umayr became a leading Companion.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r2.anchor: فأما عمير فكان من أعظم المؤذين للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولمن آمن به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r3.claim: The Prophet's call gave al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿĀmir al-Dawsī a light as a sign; he called his family and people, and none of his people held back from Islam.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r3.anchor: وكذا ذو النور الطفيل بن عامر الدوسي رضي الله عنه ثم قومه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r4.claim: For people beyond the Companions, the Prophet's traces purify according to their receptivity and God's preparation; stronger longing brings firmer adherence to Qur'an and Sunna and deeper knowledge and practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r4.anchor: وأما غير الصحابة رضي الله عنهم فتزكيته لهم بآثاره بحسب القابليات والأمور التي قضى الله أن يكون مهيأ

BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r5.claim: The Book is the revelation sent to the Prophet, gathering every kind of religious and worldly good in this life and the next.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r5.anchor: ويعلمهم الكتاب } اي المنزل عليه الجامع لكل خير ديني ودنيوي

BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r6.claim: Wisdom is the Book's goal: understanding joined to practice, and practice mastered by transmitted and rational knowledge, so each matter is placed well and they avoid Israel's deviation; this teaching alone would suffice as a miracle.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r6.anchor: وهي غاية الكتاب في قوة فهمه والعمل به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r7.claim: Because unlettered status can imply misguidance, and many thought themselves on a sound religion, وإن emphasizes that they truly were in misguidance before the Prophet, despite the possibility of later straying again.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p593/r7.anchor: وكان كثير منهم حال إنزال هذه السورة يعتقد أنهم على دين متين وحال جليل مبين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r1.claim: Before the Messenger came, the Arabs had abandoned the religion of their forefather Ismāʿīl and worshipped idols; their misguidance was plain.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r1.anchor: { من قبل } أي قبل إرساله إليهم من حين غيروا دين أبيهم إسماعيل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r2.claim: Their misguidance appeared in obvious false beliefs, widespread ignorance willingly embraced, and scorn for those who sought learning and insight, as with Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r2.anchor: باعتقادهم الأباطيل الظاهرة وظنهم أنهم على شيء وعموم الجهل لهم ورضاهم به واختيارهم له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r3.claim: This description rules out human instruction of the Prophet, magnifies his inimitable revelation, and shows how urgently they needed a messenger to guide and rescue them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p594/r3.anchor: فوصفهم بهذا غاية في نفي التعلم من مخلوق عن نبيهم إعظاما لما جاء به من الإعجاز

DURR-FULL:v8p152/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r1.claim: Qatāda says the Arab people were an unlettered community without a book to read, so God sent Muḥammad as mercy and guidance to guide them.
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} الآية قال: كان هذا الحي من العرب أمة أمية ليس فيها كتاب يقرأونه

DURR-FULL:v8p152/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r2.claim: The Prophet describes the community as unlettered: it neither writes nor calculates.
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r2.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إنا أمة أمية لا نكتب ولا نحسب

DURR-FULL:v8p152/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the Messenger as Muḥammad, the verses as the Qur'an, and the earlier manifest error as polytheism.
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} قال: هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم {يتلو عليهم آياته} قال: القرآن

DURR-FULL:v8p152/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r4.claim: Mujāhid identifies the unlettered people as the Arabs and the later people who have not joined them as the Persians.
DURR-FULL:v8p152/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} قال: العرب {وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم} قال: العجم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3355/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3355/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3355/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the ummiyyin as the Arabs.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3355/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله : هو الذي بعث في الاميين رسولا منهم قال : العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p210/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p210/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p210/r1.claim: In “wa-in,” in is the lightened form of the heavy particle and does not govern its noun or predicate; kana fills the expected place, and the lām distinguishes it from negative in.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p210/r1.anchor: و { إن } مخففة من الثقيلة وهي مهملة عن العمل في اسمها وخبرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p210/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p210/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p210/r5.claim: The clause “though they were before in clear error” is parenthetical, either between the coordinated elements or between the pronouns and the comitative object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p210/r5.anchor: وجملة { وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين } ( الجمعة : 2 ) معترضة بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p211/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p211/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p211/r7.claim: The verse establishes that the Prophet’s message is universal and addressed to all nations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p211/r7.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على عموم رسالة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لجميع الأمم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r2.claim: The ummiyyūn are the Arabs; an ummī is someone who neither reads nor writes a book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r2.anchor: والأميين: يراد بهم العرب، والأمي في اللغة الذي لا يكتب ولا يقرأ كتابا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r3.claim: One derivation links ummī to umm, mother: the person remains in the original state of a child in the womb, without literacy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r3.anchor: قيل هو منسوب إلى الأم، أي هو على الخلقة الأولى في بطن أمه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r4.claim: Another derivation links ummī to ummah, meaning the ordinary human disposition before instruction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r4.anchor: وقيل هو منسوب إلى الأمة، أي على سليقة البشر دون تعلم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r5.claim: The derivation from Umm al-Qurā, Mecca, is weak because it would restrict the description to Quraysh, whereas all Arabs are meant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r5.anchor: لأن الوصف ب الأميين على هذا يقف على قريش، وإنما المراد جميع العرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r6.claim: The Prophet calls the community unlettered: they do not calculate or write, and the month is counted as so many days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r6.anchor: وفيهم قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إنا أمة أمية لا نحسب ولا نكتب الشهر هكذا وهكذا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r7.claim: The verse enumerates God's favors to the Arabs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r7.anchor: وهذه الآية تعديد نعمة الله عندهم فيما أولاهم، والآية المتلوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r8.claim: Purifying them means cleansing them of idolatry and causing goodness to grow among them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r8.anchor: والآية المتلوة: القرآن يزكيهم معناه: يطهرهم من الشرك ويمني الخير فيهم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r9.claim: The Book is the recited revelation, and wisdom is the Sunna, the Prophet's teaching.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r9.anchor: والكتاب: الوحي المتلو، والحكمة: السنة التي هي لسانه عليه السلام،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r10.claim: Mentioning their prior manifest error reinforces the favor by contrasting their former state with guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p306#2/r10.anchor: ثم أظهر تعالى تأكيد النعمة بذكر حالهم التي كانت في الضد من الهداية، وذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r1.claim: The unlettered people are the Arabs, who did not write; Ibn al-Jawzi refers to his explanation at 2:78.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r1.anchor: يعني العرب وكانوا لا يكتبون وقد شرحنا هذا المعنى في البقرة 78

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r2.claim: The messenger is Muhammad, from their people in both kind and lineage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r2.anchor: رسولا يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم أي من جنسهم ونسبهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r3.claim: One reason for blessing them with an unlettered prophet is that his coming matches the earlier prophecies in the scriptures of the prophets.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r3.anchor: أحدها لموافقة ما تقدمت البشارة به في كتب الأنبياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r4.claim: Another reason is that his circumstances resembled theirs, making them more likely to accept him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r4.anchor: والثاني لمشاكلة حاله لأحوالهم فيكون أقرب لموافقتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r5.claim: A third reason is to prevent suspicion that he had learned the earlier scriptures.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r5.anchor: والثالث لئلا يظن به أنه يعلم كتب من قبله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r6.claim: He refers back to al-Baqara 2:129 for the preceding teaching and explains their former manifest error as idolatry.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p257#2/r6.anchor: وما بعد هذا في سورة البقرة 129 إلى قوله تعالى وإن كانوا من قبل أي وما كانوا قبل بعثته إلا في ضلال مبين بين وهو الشرك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r3.claim: The ummiyyun are the Arabs, as in the address to the people of Scripture and the unlettered in 3:20.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r3.anchor: الأميون هم: العرب كما قال تعالى: {وقل للذين أوتوا الكتاب والأميين أأسلمتم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r4.claim: Specifically naming the Arabs does not exclude other peoples; the favor was more emphatic for them as the first recipients, while other verses make the Prophet's mission universal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r4.anchor: وتخصيص الأميين بالذكر لا ينفي من عداهم، ولكن المنة عليهم أبلغ وآكد، كما في قوله: {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} [الزخرف: 44]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r5.claim: The verse fulfills Abraham's prayer that a messenger be raised among Mecca's people to recite God's signs, purify them, and teach scripture and wisdom; God sent him after a long break in prophethood when paths had faded.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية هي مصداق إجابة الله لخليله إبراهيم، حين دعا لأهل مكة أن يبعث الله فيهم رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r6.claim: Before Muhammad, most people were deeply astray; only a very small remnant among the People of Scripture still followed what God had sent Jesus.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r6.anchor: ممن تمسك بما بعث الله به عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r7.claim: Arabs had altered Abraham's monotheistic religion into idolatry and doubt, while the two scriptural communities had altered, distorted, and reinterpreted their books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r7.anchor: فبدلوه وغيروه، وقلبوه وخالفوه، واستبدلوا بالتوحيد شركا (3) وباليقين شكا، وابتدعوا أشياء لم يأذن بها الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r8.claim: God sent Muhammad with a complete law for all creation, clarifying what people need in this life and the next, guiding them toward Paradise and God's approval, and warning them away from Hell and divine anger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r8.anchor: بشرع عظيم كامل شامل لجميع الخلق، فيه هدايتهم، والبيان لجميع ما يحتاجون إليه من أمر معاشهم ومعادهم، والدعوة لهم إلى ما يقربهم إلى الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r9.claim: The prophetic message resolves doubts in both fundamentals and branches, gathers the excellences of earlier messengers, and grants Muhammad distinctions no one before or after him receives.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p115#2/r9.anchor: حاكم، فاصل لجميع الشبهات والشكوك والريب في الأصول والفروع. وجمع له تعالى، وله الحمد والمنة، جميع المحاسن ممن كان قبله

BURSEVI:v9p414/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r1.claim: The Messenger is from the unlettered people's own community and lineage, an Arab and unlettered like them.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r1.anchor: أي من جملتهم ونسبهم عربيا أميا مثلهم

BURSEVI:v9p414/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r2.claim: His likeness to them is a favor: it shows he did not learn from books, while they knew his lineage and circumstances.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r2.anchor: فوجه الامتنان مشاكلة حاله لأحوالهم ونفي التعلم من الكتب

BURSEVI:v9p414/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r3.speaker: شعيا عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p414/r3.claim: The book of Isaiah is quoted as foretelling that God would send an unlettered messenger among the unlettered and seal the prophets through him.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r3.anchor: ودر كتاب شعيا عليه السلام مذكور است كه انى ابعث أميا في الأميين واختم به النبيين

BURSEVI:v9p414/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p414/r4.claim: Al-Kāshifī's three Persian couplets praise the Prophet's unletteredness: God named him unlettered though he received the Mother of the Book, and without schooling he revealed the Tablet's secrets; the final couplet's wording is corrupt.

BURSEVI:v9p414/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r5.claim: Being sent among the unlettered does not limit the Prophet's universal mission; even if it implied a restriction, the explicit statement that he was sent to all people overrides it, refuting the People of the Book's claim that he was only for Arabs.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r5.anchor: والبعث في الأميين لا ينافي عموم دعوته عليه السلام فالتخصيص بالذكر لا مفهوم له

BURSEVI:v9p414/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r6.claim: The Messenger recites the Qurʾān to them despite being unlettered and having no prior practice in reading or learning; tilāwa is sequential recitation like study or regular litanies, while qirāʾa more broadly means voicing letters.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r6.anchor: والفرق بين التلاوة والقرآن أن التلاوة قراءة القرآن متتابعة كالدراسة والأوراد المظفة والقراءة أعم

BURSEVI:v9p414/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r7.claim: As another attribute of the Messenger, he leads people to become pure of corrupt beliefs and deeds.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r7.anchor: صفة أخرى لرسولا معطوفة على يتلو أي يحملهم على ما يصيرون به أزكياء من خبائث العقائد والأعمال

BURSEVI:v9p414/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r8.claim: This signals the Sufi path: God is the true purifier, yet the Perfect Human manifests divine attributes; the source supports this with 4:49 and 4:80.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r8.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى قاعدة التسليك فإن المزكي في الحقيقة وإن كان هو الله تعالى كما قال بل الله يزكي من يشاء

BURSEVI:v9p414/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r9.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v9p414/r9.claim: Al-Irshād says teaching follows recitation in existence, with purification placed between them because it perfects the practical soul after recitation perfects the theoretical faculty through knowledge; this ordering shows that each benefit is a distinct bounty deserving thanks.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r9.anchor: قال في الإرشاد صفة أخرى لرسولا مترتبة في الوجود على التلاوة وإنما وسط بينهما التزكية

BURSEVI:v9p414/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r10.claim: Some explain the Book and Wisdom as the Qurʾān and the revealed law, or as its wording and meaning.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ويعلمهم القرآن والشريعة وهي ما شرع الله لعباده من الأحكام

BURSEVI:v9p414/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r11.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v9p414/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets them as the Qurʾān and Sunna.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r11.anchor: أو القرآن والسنة كما قاله الحسن

BURSEVI:v9p414/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v9p414/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the Book as writing.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r12.anchor: أو الكتاب الخط كما قاله ابن عباس

BURSEVI:v9p414/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r13.speaker: ابن إسحاق
BURSEVI:v9p414/r13.claim: Ibn Isḥāq interprets the Book as knowledge of good and evil.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r13.anchor: أو الخير والشر كما قاله ابن إسحاق

BURSEVI:v9p414/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r16.claim: The terms also encompass the legal rulings of the Sharīʿa and the refined practices of the spiritual path, with their combined wisdom.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r16.anchor: أو كتاب أحكام الشريعة وأسرار آداب الطريقة وحاصل معانيه الحكمية

BURSEVI:v9p414/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r17.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r17.claim: The Qurʾān's realities and wisdom are taught fully to people of understanding, including select Companions and later generations; the Prophet taught Companions directly and later believers through the community's perfected inheritors.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r17.anchor: ولكن تعليم حقائق القرآن وحكمه مختص بأولى الفهم وهم خواص الأصحاب رضي الله عنهم وخواص التابعين

BURSEVI:v9p414/r18.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p414/r18.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p414/r18.claim: The Prophet's teaching of the Qurʾān's realities and wisdom would alone suffice as a miracle.
BURSEVI:v9p414/r18.anchor: ولو لم يكن سوى هذا التعليم معجزة لكفاه

BURSEVI:v9p415/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p415/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p415/r1.claim: Al-Būṣī's Burda line says the Prophet's knowledge while unlettered in the age of ignorance is sufficient evidence of his miracle, as is his instruction in manners while an orphan.

BURSEVI:v9p415/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p415/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p415/r2.claim: In is the lightened emphatic particle, not conditional or negative; the lām marks the difference from a negative construction.
BURSEVI:v9p415/r2.anchor: إن ليست شرطية ولا نافية بل هي المخففة واللام هر الفارقة بينها وبين النافية

BURSEVI:v9p415/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p415/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p415/r3.claim: Before the Prophet's mission the unlettered people were in manifest error through idolatry and the impurities of the pre-Islamic age; this shows their need for a guide and rebuts the idea that he learned from them.
BURSEVI:v9p415/r3.anchor: والمعنى وأن الشأن كان الأميون من قبل بعثته ومجيئه لفي ضلال مبين من الشرك وخبث الجاهلية

BURSEVI:v9p415/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p415/r4.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v9p415/r4.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī says attributing error to everyone is by predominance, since Waraqa b. Nawfal, Zayd b. ʿAmr, and Quss b. Sāʿida were guided and, according to the Prophet, each would be raised as a community alone.
BURSEVI:v9p415/r4.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : والظاهر أن نسبة الكون في الضلال إلى الجميع من باب التغليب

BURSEVI:v9p415/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p415/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p415/r5.claim: The author rejects that qualification: those men were guided in monotheism but remained astray concerning revealed laws and rulings; being guided in one respect does not conflict with error in another.
BURSEVI:v9p415/r5.anchor: يقول الفقير : هو اعتراض على معنى الإزاحة المذكورة لكنه ليس بشيء فإن اهتداء من ذكره

BURSEVI:v9p415/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p415/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p415/r6.claim: The author cites 93:7 but says it does not imply the Prophet ever committed idolatry or other sins; recitation and instruction gave purification and rescue from error in its full sense.
BURSEVI:v9p415/r6.anchor: فقد كانوا في ضلال من الشرائع والأحكام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r1.claim: The unlettered people among whom the Messenger was sent are the Arabs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r1.anchor: يعني في العرب , وفي تسميتهم أميين قولان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Arabs are called unlettered because no book was sent down to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r2.anchor: لأنه لم ينزل عليهم كتاب , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r3.claim: Qatada says they are called unlettered because they did not write and had no scribe among them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r3.anchor: لأنهم لم يكونوا يكتبون ولا كان فيهم كاتب , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r4.claim: One view limits the unlettered people here to Quraysh, who did not write until some learned from the people of al-Hira late in the pre-Islamic period.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r4.anchor: أنهم قريش خاصة لأنها لم تكن تكتب حتى تعلم بعضها في آخر الجاهلية من أهل الحيرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r5.speaker: المفضل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r5.claim: Al-Mufaddal says the term includes all Arabs because they had no scripture and only a few could write.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r5.anchor: أنهم جميع العرب لأنه لم يكن لهم كتاب ولا كتب منهم إلا قليل , قاله المفضل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r6.claim: Sending an unlettered prophet fulfilled the earlier prophets' glad tidings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r6.anchor: لموافقته ما تقدمت بشارة الأنبياء به

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r7.claim: His state resembled theirs, making them more likely to accept him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r7.anchor: حالِه لأحوالهم , فيكون أقرب إلى موافقتهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r8.claim: His being unlettered also removed suspicion that he had learned the books and wisdom he recited from texts he had read.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r8.anchor: لينتفي عنه سوء الظن في تعلمه ما دعا إليه من الكتب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r9.claim: The signs he recites to them are the Quran.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says he purifies them by making their hearts pure through faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r10.anchor: أزكياء القلوب بالإيمان , وهو معنى قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r11.speaker: ابن جريج ومقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil say he purifies them from disbelief and sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r11.anchor: يطهرهم من الكفر والذنوب ، قاله ابن جريج ومقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r12.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r12.claim: Al-Suddi interprets purification as taking the zakat of their deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r12.anchor: الثالث : يأخذ زكاة أعمالهم ، قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r13.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r13.claim: Hasan says the Book is the Quran.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Book is writing with a pen, which spread among Arabs through the religious command to record things in writing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r14.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ، لأن الخط إنما فشا في العرب بالشرع

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r15.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r15.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq says it is knowledge of good and evil through the Book, so people do good and refrain from evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r15.anchor: معرفة الخير والشر كما يعرفونه بالكتاب ليفعلوا الخير ويكفوا عن الشر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r16.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r16.claim: Hasan interprets wisdom as the Sunna.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r17.speaker: مالك بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r17.claim: Malik ibn Anas interprets wisdom as understanding jurisprudence in religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r17.anchor: أنه الفقه في الدين , وهو قول مالك بن أنس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r18.speaker: الأعمش
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p5/r18.claim: Al-Amash says wisdom is understanding and taking admonition.

MUQATIL:62:1-4/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r3.claim: The unlettered people are the Arabs, who neither read scripture nor write by hand.
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r3.anchor: يعني العرب الذين لا يقرءون الكتاب ولا يكتبون بأيديهم

MUQATIL:62:1-4/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r4.claim: The messenger sent among them is the Prophet Muhammad.
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r4.anchor: فهو النبي صلى الله عليه سلم

MUQATIL:62:1-4/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r5.claim: The messenger recites to them the verses of the Quran.
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r5.anchor: { يتلو عليهم } يعني يقرأ عليهم { آياته } يعني آيات القرآن

MUQATIL:62:1-4/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r6.claim: He purifies them by reforming them so that they affirm God's oneness.

MUQATIL:62:1-4/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r7.claim: He teaches them the Quran he recites and its admonition, including what is lawful and unlawful.
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r7.anchor: { ويعلمهم الكتاب } يعني ولكي يعلمهم ما يتلو من القرآن { والحكمة } وموعظ القرآن الحلال والحرام

MUQATIL:62:1-4/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r8.claim: Before Muhammad's commissioning, they were in manifest error, meaning polytheism.
MUQATIL:62:1-4/r8.anchor: { وإن } يعني وقد { كانوا من قبل } أن يبعث محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم { لفي ضلال مبين } [آية: 2] يعني بين وهو الشرك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r1.claim: God sent an unlettered man among an unlettered people; “from them” can also mean from their own people, whose lineage and circumstances he knew.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r1.anchor: أي بعث رجلا أميا في قوم أميين وقيل منهم كقوله من انفسكم يعلمون نسبه وأحواله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r2.claim: “Unlettered” derives from the Arab nation, who did not write or read as other nations did.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r2.anchor: والأمي منسوب إلى أمة العرب لأنهم كانوا لا يكتبون ولا يقرؤون من بين الأمم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r3.claim: Writing began in al-Ṭāʾif; its people learned it from the people of al-Ḥīra, who learned it from the people of al-Anbār.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r3.anchor: وقيل بدئت الكتابة بالطائف وهم أخذوها من ا هل ال حيرة وأهل الحيرة من اهل الأنبار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r4.claim: The verses he recites are the Qurʾān.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r5.claim: He purifies them from associating partners with God and from the vices of pre-Islamic ignorance.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r6.anchor: ويعلمهم الكتاب ﴾ القرآن ﴿ والحكمة ﴾ السنة أو الفقه في الدين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r7.claim: Wisdom can mean the Sunna or understanding of religion.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r8.claim: Before Muḥammad, they were in manifest error: disbelief and ignorance, with no error greater than theirs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r8.anchor: من قبل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ لفي ضلال مبين ﴾ كفر و جهالة وإن مخففة من الثقيلة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r9.claim: “In” is lightened from the emphatic particle; the lām signals it, and the sense is “they were in clear error.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p244#2/r9.anchor: وإن مخففة من الثقيلة واللام دليل عليها أي كانوا في ضلال

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the ummiyyun are all Arabs, literate or not, because they were not People of Scripture.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الأميون العرب كلهم، من كتب منهم ومن لم يكتب

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r2.claim: Another view defines the ummiyyun as those who do not write; Quraysh are given as an example.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r2.anchor: وقيل: الأميون الذين لايكتبون. وكذلك كانت قريش

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r3.claim: Ibrahim, as transmitted by Mansur, defines an ummi as one who can read but cannot write.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r3.anchor: وروى منصور عن إبراهيم قال: الأمي الذي يقرأ ولا يكتب

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r4.claim: The messenger sent among them is Muhammad; every Arab tribe had kinship with him and ancestry from him, except Taghlib, whom God kept from his lineage because of their Christianity, according to Ibn Ishaq.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r4.anchor: يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم. وما من حي من العرب إلا ولرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيهم قرابة

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Taghlib was excluded from the Prophet's Arab ancestry because of its Christianity, so God did not make them his forebears.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r5.anchor: إلا حي تغلب فإن الله تعالى طهر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم لنصرانيتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r6.claim: Muhammad was unlettered: he had not read from a book or studied one.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r6.anchor: وكان أميا لم يقرأ من كتاب ولم يتعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r7.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r7.claim: Al-Mawardi gives three reasons an unlettered prophet is a blessing: this matches earlier prophetic glad tidings, resembles the people's circumstances and aids their acceptance, and removes suspicion that he learned revealed books and wisdom by reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r7.anchor: قال الماوردي: فإن قيل ما وجه الامتنان فإن بعث نبيا أميا؟ فالجواب عنه من ثلاثة أوجه

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r8.claim: Qurtubi says all three reasons demonstrate Muhammad's miracle and the truth of his prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r8.anchor: قلت: وهذا كله دليل معجزته وصدق نبوته

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r9.claim: The signs the Messenger recites to them are the Qurʾan.

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains purification as making their hearts pure through faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r10.anchor: { ويزكيهم } أي يجعلهم أزكياء القلوب بالإيمان قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r11.speaker: ابن جريج، مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil explain purification as cleansing them of the filth of disbelief and sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r11.anchor: وقيل: يطهرهم من دنس الكفر والذنوب قاله ابن جريج ومقاتل

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r12.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r12.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the phrase as the Messenger taking their alms.

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r13.claim: The book taught by the Messenger is the Qurʾan.

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r14.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r14.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the wisdom taught by the Messenger as the Sunna.

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the book as writing with a pen, which spread among Arabs through the religious command to record matters in writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «الكتاب» الخط بالقلم لأن الخط فشا في العرب بالشرع

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r16.speaker: مالك بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r16.claim: Malik ibn Anas defines wisdom as understanding jurisprudence in religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r16.anchor: وقال مالك بن أنس: «الحكمة» الفقه في الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r17.claim: 'Before' means before the Messenger or before he was sent to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r17.anchor: أي من قبله وقبل أن يرسل إليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:62:2/r18.claim: Their manifest error was being far from the truth.

RAZI-FULL:v30p4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4/r3.claim: After completing discussion of divine oneness and transcendence, the passage turns to prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4/r3.anchor: بعدما فرغ من التوحيد والتنزيه شرع في النبوة

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r1.claim: Al-ummiyyūn refers to the Arab nation, an unlettered people without a scripture who neither read nor write books.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r1.anchor: الأمي منسوب إلى أمة العرب ، لما أنهم أمة أميون لا كتاب لهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the term means people who had neither a scripture nor a prophet sent among them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : يريد الذين ليس لهم كتاب ولا نبي بعث فيهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r3.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the unlettered as those remaining in the state in which they were created.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : الأميون الذين هم على ما خلقوا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r4.claim: A reading has al-amīn, omitting the yāʾ of the nisbah adjective.

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r5.claim: The Messenger is from their lineage and their kind, as other verses say that messengers came from their own people.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r5.anchor: نسبه من نسبهم ، وهو من جنسهم ، كما قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r6.claim: The people of meaning say Muhammad himself was unlettered like his people, as prior scriptures foretold; this makes reliance on writing an unlikely explanation for his wisdom and better shows the truth of his mission.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#2/r6.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : وكان هو صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا أميا مثل الأمة التي بعث فيهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r1.claim: The signs recited to the people are manifest proofs of the Messenger's mission and prophethood; they may also be the signs that set out legal rulings and distinguish truth from falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r1.anchor: أي بيناته التي تبين رسالته وتظهر نبوته ،

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r2.claim: The Messenger purifies them of the filth of associationism and other vile words and deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r2.anchor: أي يطهرهم من خبث الشرك ، وخبث ما عداه

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r3.claim: Another view reads purification as reform: calling people to follow what makes them pure and pious.

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r4.claim: One explanation takes the Book as the recited verses and wisdom as the religious obligations.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r4.anchor: والكتاب : ما يتلى من الآيات ، والحكمة : هي الفرائض

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r5.claim: Another view says wisdom means the Sunnah, which the Prophet taught alongside reciting the verses.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : { الحكمة } السنة ، لأنه كان يتلو عليهم آياته

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r6.claim: Another account takes the Book as the explicit verses and wisdom as the meanings embedded within them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r6.anchor: وقيل : { الكتاب } الآيات نصا ، والحكمة ما أودع فيها من المعاني

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r7.claim: A further possibility is that the Book is the Qur'an's verses and wisdom is the proper way of adhering to them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r7.anchor: الكتاب آيات القرآن والحكمة وجه التمسك بها

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r8.claim: Before the Messenger, they were idol worshippers in manifest error, namely associationism; he called them to divine oneness and to abandon their former way.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r8.anchor: لأنهم كانوا عبدة الأصنام وكانوا في ضلال مبين وهو الشرك ،

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r9.speaker: أهل الكتاب
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r9.claim: The People of the Book argue that specifying a Messenger among the unlettered means he was sent only to the Arabs.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r9.anchor: احتجاج أهل الكتاب بها قالوا قوله :

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects their inference: mentioning a group does not exclude others, just as saying one does not write with the right hand does not imply writing with the left.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r10.anchor: فإنه لا يلزم من تخصيص الشيء بالذكر نفي ما عداه ، ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r11.claim: The Prophet was sent to all people: the assertion that he is a bearer of good news and warner to all people rules out an Arab-only mission.
RAZI-FULL:v30p4#3/r11.anchor: ولأنه لو كان رسولا إلى العرب خاصة كان قوله تعالى :

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r1.claim: Ummī means someone unable to read or write.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r1.anchor: indicates those who can neither read nor write

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r2.claim: Ṭ takes the unlettered in this context to mean the idolatrous Arabs, who had no scripture.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r2.anchor: in this context can refer to the idolatrous Arabs, who had no scripture (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r3.claim: R offers the broader referent of anyone without a Divine book.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r3.anchor: or to anyone without a Divine book (R; cf. 3:20)

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r4.speaker: JJ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r4.claim: JJ and Ṭs understand the Prophet's purification of the people as purification from idolatry.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r4.anchor: Purifying them refers to purification from idolatry (JJ, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r5.claim: The Prophet's teaching of Book and Wisdom is linked to the primordial covenant with all prophets, who were to believe in and help a confirming messenger.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r5.anchor: the teaching of which is part of the primordial covenant made with all prophets

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r6.claim: Other verses also describe the Prophet teaching the Book and Wisdom.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r6.anchor: This is one of several verses in which the Prophet is said to teach the Book and Wisdom

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r7.claim: The teaching of Book and Wisdom is also associated with Abraham, Jesus, and Muhammad.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r7.anchor: The teaching of the Book and Wisdom is also mentioned in relation to Abraham (4:54), Jesus (5:110), and Muhammad (4:113)

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r8.claim: Some interpret Wisdom here as a reference to the Prophet's sunna.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r8.anchor: some interpret Wisdom as a reference

STUDYQURAN:62:2/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r9.claim: Wisdom may also mean all divinely inspired knowledge concerning this world and the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:62:2/r9.anchor: all Divinely inspired knowledge pertaining to this world and the Hereafter (Ṭs)

QUSHAYRI:v3p318/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p318/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p318/r1.claim: When God's beauty appears to a servant's heart, its thoughts gather around divine generosity; when His majesty appears to the secret heart, the self is consumed in Him and forgets this world and the hereafter.
QUSHAYRI:v3p318/r1.anchor: إذا تجلى لقلب عبد بوصف جماله تجمعت أفكاره على بساط جوده فلم يتفرق بسواه . ومن تجلى لسره بنعت جلاله اندرجت جملته ، واستهلك في وجوده

QUSHAYRI:v3p318/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p318/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p318/r6.claim: God made Muhammad unlettered and free from acquired learning, then raised him above all with noble qualities; as an orphan He sheltered him, and likewise gave him knowledge without study, clothing him in honor and manifesting realities through him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p318/r6.anchor: جرده كل تكلف لتعلم ، وعن الاتصاف بتطلب . ثم بعثه فيهم وأظهر عليه من الأوصاف ما فاق الجميع

TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r1.claim: The pronoun هو refers back to God's name.
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} [الجمعة: 2] قال: العرب

TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r2.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the ummiyyun in this verse as the Arabs.
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} [الجمعة: 2] قال: كان هذا الحي من العرب أمة أمية

TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the ummiyyun as Arabs; a second transmission from Sufyan likewise attributes this explanation to Mujahid.
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} [الجمعة: 2] قال: العرب

TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r4.claim: Qatada says the Arabs were an ummi community with no book to read, and God sent Muhammad as mercy and guidance to guide them.
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} [الجمعة: 2] قال: كان هذا الحي من العرب أمة أمية

TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says Muhammad's community is called ummiyyun because no scripture was sent down to them.
TAB-FULL:v22p625#3/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} [الجمعة: 2] قال: إنما سميت

TAB-FULL:v22p627/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r1.claim: The Book is God's scripture with His commands and prohibitions and the ordinances of religion.
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} [الجمعة: 2] أي: السنة

TAB-FULL:v22p627/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r2.claim: Al-Tabari explains wisdom here as the Sunna.
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} [الجمعة: 2] أي: السنة

TAB-FULL:v22p627/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r3.claim: Qatada likewise glosses the Book and wisdom as scripture and the Sunna.
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} [الجمعة: 2] أي: السنة

TAB-FULL:v22p627/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Prophet purifies people through the Book and righteous deeds, and teaches the Book and wisdom to later believers as he did to the first community.
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، قال: {ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} [الجمعة: 2] أيضا كما علم هؤلاء

TAB-FULL:v22p627/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the successive Muslim community as extending to the Hour and cites the later believers praying for those who preceded them in faith.
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r5.anchor: والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا

TAB-FULL:v22p627/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the earliest generations contained many of the foremost, while the later generations contained fewer, citing the groups of the brought-near and the people of the right hand.
TAB-FULL:v22p627/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، قال: {ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} [الجمعة: 2] أيضا كما علم هؤلاء

TUSTARI:62:2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:62:2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:62:2/r1.claim: The 'unlettered' are those who affirm Muhammad and are ascribed to him because they follow and emulate him; one who does not emulate him is not of his community.
TUSTARI:62:2/r1.anchor: الأميون هم الذين صدقوا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABATABAI:62:1-2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-2/r9.claim: The opening glorification lays a rational foundation for the mission that perfects, guides, and makes people happy after their manifest error.
TABATABAI:62:1-2/r9.anchor: من بعثة الرسول لتكميل الناس وإسعادهم وهدايتهم بعد إذ كانوا في ضلال مبين

TABATABAI:62:2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r1.claim: Ummiyyin means people who cannot read or write.
TABATABAI:62:2/r1.anchor: الأميون جمع أمي وهو الذي لا يقرأ ولا يكتب

TABATABAI:62:2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r2.claim: The likely referent is the Arabs, since few among them could read or write; Muhammad was one of their kind, while also being sent to all humanity.
TABATABAI:62:2/r2.anchor: المراد بهم - كما قيل - العرب لقلة من كان منهم يقرأ ويكتب وقد كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم منهم

TABATABAI:62:2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r3.claim: The proposal that ummiyyin means non-Jews or other People of the Book does not fit, since the Prophet's message was not limited in that way.
TABATABAI:62:2/r3.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يناسب قوله في ذيل الآية

TABATABAI:62:2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r4.claim: The proposal that it means Meccans, named for Mecca as Umm al-Qura, is unsuitable for a Medinan surah and its pronoun reference.
TABATABAI:62:2/r4.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يناسب كون السورة مدنية لإيهامه كون ضمير

TABATABAI:62:2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r5.claim: Being from the ummiyyin and initially sent among them is compatible with being sent to them and to all other peoples.
TABATABAI:62:2/r5.anchor: ولا منافاة بين كونه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من الأميين مبعوثا فيهم وبين كونه مبعوثا إليهم وإلى غيرهم

TABATABAI:62:2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r6.claim: The Prophet first recited and taught in Arabic as the initial stage of his mission; after it gained stability he addressed Jews, Christians, Magians, and rulers.
TABATABAI:62:2/r6.anchor: ولذا لما استقرت الدعوة بعض الاستقرار أخذ صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يدعو اليهود والنصارى والمجوس وكاتب العظماء والملوك

TABATABAI:62:2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r7.claim: Abraham and Ishmael's prayer covers all descendants of Ishmael, including Mudar Arabs beyond Mecca, without limiting the Prophet's mission to them alone.
TABATABAI:62:2/r7.anchor: تشمل جميع آل إسماعيل من عرب مضر أعم من أهل مكة وغيرهم

TABATABAI:62:2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r8.claim: The Prophet recites the verses of the Book despite being unlettered; this phrase describes the messenger.
TABATABAI:62:2/r8.anchor: أي آيات كتابه مع كونه أميا

TABATABAI:62:2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r9.claim: Tazkiya derives from growth that is wholesome, good, and blessed; the Prophet cultivates people in that way.
TABATABAI:62:2/r9.anchor: التزكية تفعيل من الزكاة بمعنى النمو الصالح الذي يلازم الخير والبركة

TABATABAI:62:2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r10.claim: By habituating people to virtuous character and good deeds, the Prophet perfects their humanity so they live and die happy.
TABATABAI:62:2/r10.anchor: فتزكيته لهم تنميته لهم نماء صالحا بتعويدهم الأخلاق الفاضلة والأعمال الصالحة

TABATABAI:62:2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r11.claim: Teaching the Book means explaining the wording of its verses and interpreting what is difficult in them.
TABATABAI:62:2/r11.anchor: وتعليم الكتاب بيان ألفاظ آياته وتفسير ما أشكل من ذلك

TABATABAI:62:2/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r12.claim: Teaching wisdom means teaching the true knowledge contained in the Qur'an.
TABATABAI:62:2/r12.anchor: ويقابله تعليم الحكمة وهي المعارف الحقيقية التي يتضمنها القرآن

TABATABAI:62:2/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
