TABATABAI:62:2/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r13.claim: One suggested explanation is that calling the Qur'an both verses and Book highlights each title as a blessing by which God favors people.
TABATABAI:62:2/r13.anchor: والتعبير عن القرآن تارة بالآيات وتارة بالكتاب للدلالة

TABATABAI:62:2/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r14.claim: Purification precedes teaching here because the verse describes the Prophet's education of believers, where ethical formation comes before true sciences.
TABATABAI:62:2/r14.anchor: لأن هذه الآية تصف تربيته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لمؤمني أمته، والتزكية مقدمة في مقام التربية

TABATABAI:62:2/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2/r15.claim: Abraham's prayer orders knowledge before purification because it asks for these qualities to be realized, and knowledge ranks earlier and higher than conduct and morals.
TABATABAI:62:2/r15.anchor: وأما ما في دعوة إبراهيم عليه السلام فإنها دعاء وسؤال أن يتحقق في ذريته هذه الزكاة والعلم بالكتاب والحكمة

TABATABAI:62:2-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2-5/r1.claim: In the phrase about their former error, in is the lightened form of the emphatic particle.
TABATABAI:62:2-5/r1.anchor: مخففة من الثقيلة والمراد أنهم كانوا من قبل بعثة الرسول

TABATABAI:62:2-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2-5/r2.claim: They were plainly astray before the Messenger's mission; the verse is praise following glorification and expresses gratitude for divine favor.
TABATABAI:62:2-5/r2.anchor: والآية تحميد بعد تسبيح ومسوقة للامتنان

TABATABAI:62:2-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:2-5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:2-5/r8.claim: The verse and the two preceding verses are framed as a statement of God's favor.

TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r1.claim: Different communities orient themselves along distinct paths, as the Qur'an says that each has a direction toward which it turns.

TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r2.claim: The nonreligious person who submits to matter turns away from preparing for eternal life and pursues worldly concerns.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r2.anchor: وغير الملي الخاضع للمادة يلوي إلى خلاف ذلك

TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r3.claim: A religious person takes eternal life into account in their efforts, prepares for permanence, and turns toward God.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r3.anchor: الملي يراعي في مساعيه جانب ما يراه لنفسه من الحياة الخالدة المؤبدة

TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r4.claim: Ways of life differ among religious and nonreligious communities and among religious traditions because their views of existence differ.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r4.anchor: ويختلف سنن هؤلاء باختلافهم أنفسهم فيما بينهم كاختلاف سنن الوثنيين من البرهميين والبوذيين وغيرهم والمليين من المجوسية والكليمية والمسيحية والمسلمين

TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r5.claim: A religious person prepares for lasting life and turns to God without excessive concern for transient attractions; a materialist follows the opposite course.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r5.anchor: الملي يراعي في مساعيه جانب ما يراه لنفسه من الحياة الخالدة المؤبدة ويذعن من الآراء بما يناسب ذلك

TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r6.claim: Because humans are materially entangled with apparent causes, they imagine worldly life and its possessions are the ultimate reality, and treat desired immediate benefits as absolute good.

TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r7.claim: People outside religion act on materialist beliefs; religious adherents may do so in practice while professing the opposite, producing an inner conflict like the Qur'anic parable.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#2/r7.anchor: فمن كان منهم من غير أهل الملة جرى على هذه الآراء ولا خبر عنده عما وراء ذلك، ومن كان منهم من أهل الملة جرى عليها عملا وهو معترف بخلافها قولا

TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r1.claim: Fitrah's cognition and inclinations move toward real perfection and happiness, grounding the true beliefs and actions taught by religion.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r1.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن الفطرة لا تهتدي علما ولا تميل عملا

TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r2.claim: Fitrah's fundamental beliefs about origin and return, derived beliefs, and actions are true because they serve real human happiness.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r2.anchor: فما تهتدي إليه من الاعتقادات الأصلية في المبدأ والمعاد

TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r3.claim: Truth is a belief matching reality and accompanied by right guidance without error; the Qur'an calls the religion and its guidance the religion of truth and guidance to truth.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r3.anchor: وليس الحق إلا الرأي والاعتقاد الذي يطابقه الواقع ويلازمه الرشد من غير غي

TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r4.claim: Wisdom is sound judgment that admits no falsehood and yields benefit without harm.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r4.anchor: الرأي الذي أحكم في صدقه فلا يتخلله كذب، وفي نفعه فلا يعقبه ضرر

TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r5.claim: Revelation joins the Book and wisdom, the Qur'an is called wise, and the Messenger is repeatedly described as teaching wisdom.

TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r6.claim: The Prophet's Qur'anic teaching clarifies true beliefs about existence and human nature, and the derivative beliefs that guide human purposes and actions.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r6.anchor: من تعليم الحكمة وشأنه بيان ما هو الحق في أصول الاعتقادات

TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r7.claim: The Qur'an corrects the view that worldly life is all there is by teaching that worldly life is play while the afterlife is true life.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#3/r7.anchor: والقرآن ينبههم بقوله وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان

TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r1.claim: Against attributing events to night and day, the Qur'an teaches that creation and command belong to God and judgment is His alone.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r1.anchor:
ألا له الخلق والأمر
الأعراف 54، وقوله
إن الحكم إلا لله
يوسف 40، وغير ذلك من آيات الحكمة

TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r2.claim: The Qur'an denies that human beings will independently, and that they can guide whom they wish without God.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r2.anchor:
ويرون أن لهم أن يطيعوا ويعصوا ويهدوا ويهتدوا والقرآن ينبئهم بقوله
إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء
القصص 56

TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r3.claim: The Qur'an rejects the belief that people possess independent strength, saying all strength is God's.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r3.anchor:
ويرون أن لهم قوة والقرآن ينكر ذلك بقوله
أن القوة لله جميعا
البقرة 165

TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r4.claim: The Qur'an rejects wealth and allies as sources of honor, declaring that honor belongs to God, His Messenger, and believers.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r4.anchor:
القرآن يحكم بخلافه بقوله
أيبتغون عندهم العزة إن العزة لله جميعا
النساء 139. وقوله
ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين

TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r5.claim: Against treating martyrdom as death and extinction, the Qur'an says those killed in God's way are alive, though people do not perceive it.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r5.anchor: والقرآن يعده حياة إذ يقول ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله أموات بل أحياء ولكن لا تشعرون

TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r6.claim: These teachings are wisdom by which the Prophet calls people, believers counsel one another to truth, and God grants great good to the wise.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r6.anchor: إلى غير ذلك من التعاليم القرآنية التي أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يدعو بها الناس قال ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة

TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r7.claim: The Qur'an recasts people's knowledge and conduct into a new form, giving them a life that never ends.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r7.anchor: فالقرآن بالحقيقة يقلب الإنسان في قالب من حيث العلم والعمل حديث ويصوغه صوغا جديدا فيحيى حياة لا يتعقبها موت أبدا

TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r8.claim: He rejects the claim that Qur'anic exegesis is merely recitation and that close study of its meanings is forbidden interpretation.
TABATABAI:62:1-8#4/r8.anchor: ومما تقدم يتبين فساد قول من قال إن تفسير القرآن تلاوته، وإن التعمق في مداليل آيات القرآن من التأويل الممنوع

TABRISI:62:2-5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:62:2-5/r2.claim: In this clause inna is the lightened form of inna; the separating lām is required in kana's predicate to distinguish it from negative in.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r2.anchor: إن هذه مخففة من إن ولهذا لزمها اللام الفارقة في خبر كان لئلا يلتبس بإن النافية

TABRISI:62:2-5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r9.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:62:2-5/r9.claim: Mujahid and Qatada identify the unlettered people as the Arabs, who neither wrote nor read and had no prophet sent to them.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r9.anchor: يعني العرب وكانت أمة أمية لا تكتب ولا تقرأ ولم يبعث إليهم نبي عن مجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:62:2-5/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:62:2-5/r10.claim: Another view identifies them as the people of Mecca, since Mecca is called the Mother of Cities.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r10.anchor: وقيل: يعني أهل مكة لان مكة تسمى أم القرى

TABRISI:62:2-5/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:62:2-5/r11.claim: The messenger is Muhammad, whose lineage and human kind are their own, as in the verse describing a messenger from among yourselves.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r11.anchor: يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم نسبه نسبهم وهو من جنسهم كما قال لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم

TABRISI:62:2-5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:62:2-5/r12.claim: Sending an unlettered prophet fulfilled earlier prophets' scriptural predictions and blocks the suspicion that he borrowed his wisdom from books he read; his accurate accounts of past nations therefore show revelation.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r12.anchor: ووجه النعمة في أنه جعل النبوة في أمي موافقته لما تقدمت البشارة به في كتب الأنبياء السالفة

TABRISI:62:2-5/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:62:2-5/r13.claim: He recites the Quran to them, containing the lawful and forbidden, proofs, and rulings.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r13.anchor: أي يقرأ عليهم القرآن المشتمل على الحلال والحرام والحجج والأحكام

TABRISI:62:2-5/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:62:2-5/r14.claim: He purifies them from unbelief and sins and calls them to what makes them pure.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r14.anchor: أي ويطهرهم من الكفر والذنوب ويدعوهم إلى ما يصيرون به أزكياء

TABRISI:62:2-5/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:62:2-5/r15.claim: The Book is the Quran and wisdom is the religious law.

TABRISI:62:2-5/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r16.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:62:2-5/r16.claim: Another view makes wisdom encompass the Quran, Sunna, and all divinely intended knowledge applied to what should be done or avoided in religion and worldly life.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r16.anchor: وقيل: إن الحكمة تعم الكتاب والسنة وكل ما أراده الله تعالى فإن الحكمة هي العلم الذي يعمل عليه

TABRISI:62:2-5/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:62:2-5/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:62:2-5/r17.claim: Before the Prophet was sent, they had plainly turned away from truth and religion.
TABRISI:62:2-5/r17.anchor: معناه وما كانوا من قبل بعثه إليهم إلا في عدول عن الحق وذهاب عن الدين بين ظاهر

THALABI:v9p305#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p305#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p305#3/r6.claim: The unlettered people among whom the messenger was sent are the Arabs, and the messenger is Muhammad.
THALABI:v9p305#3/r6.anchor: هو الذي بعث في الأميين يعني العرب رسولا منهم محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم يتلوا عليهم آياته

THALABI:v9p305#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p305#3/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p305#3/r7.claim: One parsing puts آخرين in the genitive, attached back to الأميين, with an implied في: among other unlettered people.
THALABI:v9p305#3/r7.anchor: وآخرين منهم في آخرين وجهان من الأعراب: أحدهما الخفض على الرد الى الأميين، مجازه: وفي آخرين،

THALABI:v9p305#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p305#3/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p305#3/r8.claim: A second parsing puts آخرين in the accusative, attached to the object pronoun in يعلمهم, meaning that the Prophet teaches other believers who follow his religion.
THALABI:v9p305#3/r8.anchor: ويعلم آخرين منهم أي من المؤمنين الذين يدينون بدينه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#3/r1.claim: The unlettered people addressed here are the Arabs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم} يعني العرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#3/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#3/r2.claim: The Arabs were a nation without a scripture, not reading books or writing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#3/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: كانت العرب أمة لا كتاب لهم، ولا يقرأون كتابا ولا يكتبون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r1.claim: The unlettered are those in the natural state of a community before learning scripture.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: الأميون الذين هم على ما خلقت عليه الأمة قبل تعلم الكتاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r2.claim: The messenger is Muḥammad: his lineage is theirs and he is one of their kind.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- نسبه نسبهم وهو من جنسهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r3.claim: His own unlettered state matched the people he was sent to, fulfilled the prior description of the unlettered Prophet, and made reliance on writing for his wisdom less plausible, supporting his truthfulness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r3.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: وكان هو -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أميا مثل أولئك الأمة الذين بعث فيهم، وكانت البشارة به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī points to his earlier explanation in Sūrat al-Baqara for the messenger’s reciting, purifying, and teaching.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p445#5/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: {يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} مفسر في سورة البقرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p446/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p446/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p446/r1.claim: Before the Messenger was sent among them, they were in manifest error: they practiced polytheism and worshiped stone idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p446/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين} أي: ما كانوا من قبل بعثه فيهم إلا في ضلال بين، وهو الشرك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r1.claim: God comprehends all things, seen and unseen, public and secret, with knowledge untouched by doubt; 6:59 is cited as evidence for His knowledge of every detail.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r1.anchor: ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r2.claim: God knows without thought, sees without eyes, creates without tools, speaks without a tongue or sound, wills without mental resolve, and governs and decrees without consultation or deliberation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r3.claim: The Messenger sent among the unlettered is from the noblest lineage, highest standing, best character, and most renowned parents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r3.anchor: بعث في الأميين رسولا من أوسطهم نسبا، وأشرفهم حسبا، وأحسنهم أدبا، وأشهرهم أما وأبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r4.claim: He recites God's signs and answers falsehood with proofs; the clear revelation dispels doubt and disbelief and rescues people from misguidance and bewilderment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r4.anchor: يتلو عليهم آياته، ويعارض أباطيلهم ببيناته، حتى انكشطت غشاوة الشك عن وجه اليقين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r5.claim: The Qur'an's Arabic raised the standing of its language, while its composition surpassed Arab eloquence; its audience failed to produce anything comparable despite their mastery of rhetoric.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r5.anchor: وجعله قرآنا عربيا فرفع به من شأن لغتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r6.claim: The author had long planned a concise work on Qur'anic meanings, parsing, obscure points, and the reasons behind variant readings, and undertook it at the urging of serious scholars.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r6.anchor: فمنذ دهر تحدثني نفسي بأن أعلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r7.claim: He laments his era's neglect of learning and its pretenders, while affirming that a small number of genuine scholars remain virtuous and that knowledge retains its honor despite being shunned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p391/r7.anchor: لتوفر دواعي أهل زماننا على الجهل، وظهور رغباتهم عن العلم، الذي فيه شرف الدين والدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:62:1-3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:62:1-3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:62:1-3/r1.anchor: هو الذي بعث في الأميين } يعني: العرب { رسولا منهم } محمدا عليه السلام.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:62:1-3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:62:1-3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:62:1-3/r2.claim: The messenger sent among them is Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:62:1-3/r2.anchor: رسولا منهم } محمدا عليه السلام. { وآخرين منهم } أي: وفي آخرين منهم

MAJAZ:v2p258/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p258/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p258/r1.claim: Al-ummiyyīn are people who cannot write.

ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r11.claim: Ummiyyin here means the Arabs. Ummī may mean one related to a mother and thus unlettered, one related to a community, or one from Mecca; Elmalılı prefers the famous first sense, confirmed by context.
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r11.anchor: Meşhur olan evvelkidir. Burada sözün gidişinden de maksad o olduğu anlaşılır.

ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r12.claim: He cites a hadith describing the community as unlettered, unable to write or calculate, as evidence for the first meaning of ummī.
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r12.anchor: diye vârid olan bir hadiste bu mânaya işaret buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r13.claim: God sent from among the Arabs, then living in ignorance, a Messenger who became a source of knowledge and wisdom, as if bringing life out of the dead.
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r13.anchor: ümmîler içinde kendilerinden bir Resul ba‘s buyurdu ki ümmîlerden murad Araplardır.

ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r14.claim: The Messenger recites God’s signs and purifies people from false beliefs and bad character, brings them spiritual flourishing, opens their minds, and makes them shine among peoples.
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r14.anchor: Üzerlerine Allah’ın âyetlerini okuyor {وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ} ve onları tezkiye ediyor bâtıl akidelerden, fena huylardan temizleyip feyizlendiriyor

ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r15.claim: Teaching the Book and wisdom includes literacy and instruction in the Qur’an, as well as the Sunnah and hadith and the transmitted and rational knowledge and practice needed to apply rulings.
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r15.anchor: ve onlara kitap ve hikmet öğretiyor okuyup yazmayı ve kitapların en yükseği olan Kur’ân’ı belletiyor. Sünen ve ehâdîs ile icrâ-yı ahkâm için naklî ve aklî ilimler ve ameller tâlim eyliyor.

ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r16.claim: Before the Messenger came, the Arabs were in manifest error, bewildered and unsure what to do.
ELMALILI:62:1-7#2/r16.anchor: bundan evvel o ümmîler açık bir dalâl içinde ne yapacaklarını bilmez şaşkın bir hâlde idiler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r1.claim: The Prophet’s duties are to recite God’s revelations by conveying revelation as received, purify people by educating them spiritually and ethically, and teach and explain the Book and wisdom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r1.anchor: Peygamberin temel görevi Allah’ın âyetlerini okuma yani aldığı vahyi olduğu gibi bildirme, insanları arındırma yani ruhen yücelmeleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r2.claim: The Messenger was sent not only to his first audience but also to people who would come later.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r2.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem’in yalnız ilk muhataplarına değil daha sonra geleceklere de elçi olarak gönderildiği belirtilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r3.claim: Sending revelation and assigning prophethood are divine favors that depend solely on God’s will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r3.anchor: peygamber ve vahiy gönderme veya peygamberlik görevi vermenin ilâhî bir lutuf olduğu, bunun da ancak Allah’ın dilemesine bağlı bulunduğu bildirilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r4.claim: Ummiyyin is explained either as Arabs, most of whom could not read or write, or as a community without its own revealed book.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r4.anchor: Ümmî kelimesi bu bağlamda, “büyük çoğunluğu okuma yazma bilmeyen Araplar” veya “kendilerine ait ilâhî bir kitabı olmayan topluluk” anlamlarıyla açıklanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r5.claim: For the Prophet’s duties and the audience’s former manifest misguidance, the commentary links this passage to al-Baqara 2:129 and 2:151 and Al ʿImran 3:164.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r5.anchor: peygamberin belirtilen görevleri ve muhatapların daha önce açık bir sapkınlık içinde olmaları hakkında bk. Bakara 2/129, 151; Âl-i İmrân 3/164

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r6.claim: The commentary refers to al-Baqara 2:269 for the meaning of “wisdom.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r7.claim: For the meanings of ummiyyin, the commentary points to al-Baqara 2:78 and Al ʿImran 3:20 and 3:75.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r7.anchor: “ümmîler” kelimesinin anlamları hakkında bk. Bakara 2/78; Âl-i İmrân 3/20, 75

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:62:2/r8.claim: For the expression “unlettered Prophet,” the commentary points to al-Aʿraf 7:157–158.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r8.claim: Al-Jumuʿah repeats ما because its following verses discuss the human recipients of the Messenger's mission and others who have not yet joined them.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r8.anchor: ويمضي في الكلام على أهل الأرض

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r1.claim: من أنفسهم conveys closer, more particular intimacy and distinction than منهم, which can merely signal group membership unless context adds honor or closeness.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r1.anchor: أن قولك: (فلان من أنفس القوم) أوقع في القرب والخصوص من قولك (فلان منهم)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r4.claim: Because الأميين includes Quraysh and other Arabs outside the People of the Book, both those who believed and those who did not, the broader منهم fits.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#3/r4.anchor: لفظ الأميين يتناول قريشاً وغيرهم من العرب ممن ليس من أهل الكتاب قيل: (منهم) فناسبت هذه الآية

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r3.claim: Ibn Jinni defends the reading with a still mīm, arguing Sibawayh accurately transmitted what he heard and that Abu al-ʿAbbās’s alternative cannot fit the poetic meter.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r3.anchor: كما في الاحتجاج لقراءة: "ويعلمهم الكتاب"1 بسكون الميم

DAMGHANI:v1p45/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p45/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p45/r1.claim: Al-ummiyyīn means the Arabs, among whom the Messenger was sent.
DAMGHANI:v1p45/r1.anchor: فوجه منها : الأمي يعني العربي . قوله تعالى في سورة الجمعة
